newsitem.title: CHINA: China to choose generators on dam project by July.
newsitem.headline: China to choose generators on dam project by July.

text.p: China is reviewing tenders from six groups for the supply of generators for the Three Gorges project, and a winner will be selected by late June or early July, officials said on Tuesday.

The groups in the running included Siemens AG and GE Canada; Anglo-French group GEC Alsthom ; Swedish-Swiss ABB ; a Russian consortium; a Japanese group; and Impsa of Argentina as well as Westinghouse of Canada, they said.
Officials of the company overseeing the project, the China Yangtze Three Gorges Project Development Corp, declined to give further details on the groups in the bidding.
The China Daily newspaper quoted Lu Youmei, president of China Yangtze Three Gorges Project Development, as saying the 14 generating units would have a total installed capacity of 9,800 megawatts.
The newspaper said bidders were required to sub-contract at least 25 percent of the work to domestic power equipment makers.
The huge hydropower and water conservancy project, which will dam the Yangtze river, is expected to be completed in 2009.
